scope: Proposition 3.1 (The initial simplex) of the manuscript “Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions” (preprints/Maximal-Multipoint-Seshadri-Constants-in-Higher-Dimensions-October-5-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 039 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dc7a580f2b1d6cf6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X be a smooth integral complex projective variety of dimension n ≥ 3, let L be ample, and put V = Ln. Choose a positive integer D such that DL is very ample. There is a graded support family Sk ⊂ Zn ≥0 such that Sk ⊂ kP0, P0 = ∆(1/D, . . . , 1/D, Dn−1 V ), (3.2) #Sk = h0 (X, kL) = V n! kn + O(kn−1 ), vol(P0) = V n! . (3.3) For all integers k ≥ 1, m ≥ 0, and r ≥ 1, if M(Sk) separates jets through degree m at some distinct r-tuple in Tn, then H0(X, kL) does so at some distinct r-tuple in X.
